source.title: Cordial elements and dimensions of affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties
source.version: Published Cambridge open-access PDF, 15 pages; read completely, including references. The arXiv PDF was acquired only for provenance/possible comparison, not used instead of the publication.
readSections: §2.1–2.2, all setup, upper bound and shrunken conventions
§5.1–5.4, normalized subtraction and entire correspondence proof
§6.1–6.5, main proof, corollary and Levi remark

summary: Full published-paper reading and itemized checkpoint for cordiality and shrunken-chamber ADLV dimension formulas. Existing local-group, Newton and affine flag owners are imported; two Part II briefs add Demazure/dominant subtraction and ADLV geometry. Explicit unresolved proof interfaces G1–G3 prevent a complete claim; no formalization is asserted.

items.name: Completed maximal unramified coefficient field
items.statement: For a nonarchimedean local field F, put L=F-breve, the completion of the maximal unramified extension in a fixed separable closure, with continuous arithmetic Frobenius σ, residue field kbar and a uniformizer inherited from F. The absolute Galois group has inertia Γ0.
items.note: API: Construct the completion and extension of Frobenius; identify fixed field, valuation and residue actions. Import finite unramified extensions/Frobenius from LocalFieldsRamification Layer 2; this item is their completed limit adapter. Tests: F=F_q((t)) gives L=kbar((t)), σ(t)=t and coefficient q-power; the mixed-characteristic unramified case uses Witt Frobenius, not coefficientwise characteristic-p arithmetic.

items.name: Local reductive root datum and affine apartment
items.statement: For connected reductive G/F choose an F-defined maximal L-split torus S containing a maximal F-split torus; T=Z_G(S). Put W0=N_G(T)(L)/T(L). The apartment is identified after choices with X_*(T)_Γ0⊗R; use the reduced root system attached to the affine Weyl group, which need not be the relative root system itself.
items.note: API: Expose torus/normalizer, relative and reduced affine root systems, pairing and σ-action; carry the choice of apartment origin. Tests: SL2; a nonsplit group with multipliable relative roots; preserve the distinction between its reduced affine root system and relative roots.

items.name: Base alcove and Iwahori
items.statement: Fix a σ-stable alcove a and its Iwahori I⊂G(L). The positive finite chamber is opposite a; t^λ acts on the apartment by v↦v−λ.
items.note: API: Alcove fixers, σ-stability, intersection with T and translation-action convention; compare parahoric group schemes. Tests: Type A1: a has α-coordinate (−1,0), t^{α∨} shifts by −2; do not silently use the opposite sign.

items.name: Iwahori–Weyl group
items.statement: Wtilde=N_G(T)(L)/(T(L)∩I), with 0→X_*(T)_Γ0→Wtilde→W0→1. A special vertex supplies a splitting Wtilde=X_*(T)_Γ0⋊W0.
items.note: API: Quotient maps, representatives, translation embedding and semidirect multiplication; record σ-compatibility under the quasi-split setup. Tests: t^λu t^μv=t^{λ+uμ}uv; torsion coinvariants cannot be erased by tensoring with R.

items.name: Affine Weyl subgroup and length-zero extension
items.statement: The affine Weyl subgroup Wa is the Coxeter group on walls of a; Wtilde=Wa⋊Ω with Ω the alcove stabilizer and length zero. Extend length and Bruhat order cosetwise to Wtilde.
items.note: API: Wa/Ω inclusion, decomposition and cosetwise order, σ-preservation and simple reflections; reuse the abstract Coxeter APIs. Tests: Different Ω-components are incomparable; a nonidentity Ω element has length zero.

items.name: Abstract Coxeter length
items.statement: For cs:CoxeterSystem M W, ℓ(w) is the minimal number of simple generators representing w, and a word is reduced iff its number of letters equals ℓ of its product.
items.note: API: Reuse reduced expressions, word product and length; this supplies the abstract carrier only, not the affine-group identification. Tests: Identity has length zero; simple generators have length one.

items.name: Coxeter length inversion and subadditivity
items.statement: For a Coxeter system and u,v∈W, ℓ(u⁻¹)=ℓ(u) and ℓ(uv)≤ℓ(u)+ℓ(v).

items.name: Abstract Bruhat order
items.statement: For a Coxeter system, u≤w is the reflexive-transitive closure of steps multiplying by a reflection and strictly increasing length. This gives a partial order.
items.note: API: Use BruhatLE, transitivity, antisymmetry and length monotonicity; an adapter supplies the extended affine Ω-components. Tests: Identity≤w; u≤w and w≤u imply equality; do not infer arbitrary subword converses from the one-direction API.

items.name: Parabolic subgroups and minimal representatives
items.statement: For K among finite or affine simple generators let W_K be the generated subgroup, {}^K W the minimal representatives for W_K\W and W^K those for W/W_K; finite K is used where a longest element is needed.
items.note: API: Membership by left/right descents, unique length-additive parabolic factorization and inversion interchange of left/right representatives. Tests: W0=S3, K={s1}; left and right representative sets differ; K=∅ and K=S.

items.name: σ-conjugacy classes and algebraic σ-centralizer
items.statement: B(G) is the quotient of G(L) by g·b=g b σ(g)⁻¹. J_b is the algebraic F-group with J_b(F)={g∈G(L):g b σ(g)⁻¹=b}, not merely that abstract subgroup.
items.note: API: Class map, conjugacy transport, J_b functor and representability/inner-Levi comparison. Tests: GL1 and basic GL2; change representative by σ-conjugation and compare centralizers.

items.name: Kottwitz and Newton invariants
items.statement: A class [b] has κ(b)∈Ω_σ≅π1(G)_Γ and a dominant rational σ-fixed Newton coweight ν_b. These classify B(G) in the stated local reductive setting, with functoriality under Levi inclusions and central maps.
items.note: API: Define κ, ν and class invariance, compare to translations and the algebraic fundamental group; distinguish a Levi-dominant vector from its G-dominant representative. Tests: GL2 diag(t,1) and diag(1,t) have the same G-class, different torus classes; torus central slopes are retained.

items.name: Defect
items.statement: def_G(b)=rank_F(G)−rank_F(J_b), with J_b the algebraic σ-centralizer.
items.note: API: Class invariance, rank computation, behavior under central/adjoint comparison and translation case. Tests: Quasi-split dominant translations have defect zero; an anisotropic basic inner form may have positive defect.

items.name: Newton partial order
items.statement: [b]≤[b′] means κ(b)=κ(b′) and ν_b≤ν_b′ in rational coroot dominance.
items.note: API: Partial-order laws, equal-κ necessity and basic minimal class in a fixed κ-fibre. Tests: Unequal κ classes are incomparable even when Newton coordinates appear ordered.

items.name: Affine flag carrier
items.statement: Fl=G(L)/I on kbar-points, represented by the corresponding equal-characteristic affine flag ind-scheme, or perfect flag geometry in mixed characteristic; the carrier and comparison must be fixed before discussing dimensions.
items.note: API: Quotient functor, bounded Schubert strata, Frobenius, group action, finite-type/perfectly finite-type models and topology/dimension comparison. Tests: Rank-one Schubert curve; distinguish a perfect scheme from a finite-type scheme. The printed equal-characteristic sentence cites BS17, whose Witt construction addresses mixed characteristic.

items.name: Iwahori–Bruhat decomposition
items.statement: G(L)=⨆_{w∈Wtilde} I wdot I; hence Fl is partitioned by I-orbits indexed by Wtilde.

items.name: Affine Deligne–Lusztig variety
items.statement: For b∈G(L), w∈Wtilde, X_w(b)={gI∈Fl:g⁻¹bσ(g)∈I wdot I}, with the reduced locally closed geometric structure inside Fl and dimension −∞ for the empty set. After §2.2 the paper assumes G simple and quasi-split.
items.note: API: Define via the relative-position graph, show independence of representatives, σ-conjugacy invariance in b and the J_b(F)-action, and construct bounded finite-dimensional pieces. Tests: X_1(1); κ mismatch forces emptiness; for GL1 the condition becomes the valuation/Kottwitz condition.

items.name: Kottwitz obstruction
items.statement: If X_w(b) is nonempty, κ(b)=κ(w).
items.note: Apply κ to g⁻¹bσ(g); the coboundary vanishes in σ-coinvariants.

items.name: Dominant double-coset normal form
items.statement: Uniquely write w=x t^λ y with λ dominant, x,y∈W0 and t^λy∈{}^S Wtilde; then ℓ(w)=ℓ(x)+ℓ(t^λ)−ℓ(y).
items.note: API: Normal form, uniqueness, conversion to semidirect coordinates, and the length formula with wall stabilizers. Tests: λ=0 forces y=1 in the minimal-representative convention; singular λ must use the specified representative rather than arbitrary x,y.

items.name: Finite twisted part
items.statement: For the preceding unique normal form define η_σ(w)=σ⁻¹(y)x∈W0.
items.note: API: Normal-form independence and formulas for x t^λ and dominant-chamber elements; length and support adapters. Tests: η(x t^λ)=x; reversing the order to xσ⁻¹(y) is not generally equal in S3.

items.name: Virtual dimension
items.statement: d_w(b)=(ℓ(w)+ℓ(η_σ(w))−def_G(b))/2−〈ν_b,ρ〉, where 〈α∨,ρ〉=1 on simple coroots.
items.note: API: Use rational-valued arithmetic before proving any integrality; difference at fixed b cancels defect/Newton terms; explicit empty-dimension conventions. Tests: For w=1,b=1 the value is zero; compare ADLV dimension with the I-normalized Newton-stratum dimension, which differs by 〈2ρ,ν_b〉.

items.name: Virtual dimension upper bound
items.statement: For G simple quasi-split in the paper’s setup, b∈G(L), w∈Wtilde, dim X_w(b)≤d_w(b), with the empty case −∞.
items.note: He14 Cor.10.4 and He15 Thm2.30 are the named inputs; the latter is formulated for I-normalized dimension of IwI∩[b], so He15 Thm2.23 supplies the subtraction of 〈2ρ,ν_b〉.

items.name: Finite and σ-saturated support
items.statement: supp(w) for w∈W0 is the set of simple generators occurring in a reduced word; supp_σ(w)=⋃_{n∈Z}σ^n(supp(w)), independent of the word.
items.note: API: Reduced-word invariance, parabolic membership, product containment, σ-saturation, inversion and diagram-automorphism behavior. Tests: Identity has empty support; a diagram automorphism can make the saturated support strictly larger.

items.name: Hodge coweight and σ-average
items.statement: λ_w is the unique dominant λ with w∈W0 t^λ W0; λ_w^♦ is the average over its finite σ-orbit in the rational coweight space.
items.note: API: Double-coset invariance, averaging independent of a multiple of the orbit order and preservation of coroot dominance. Tests: Split σ gives λ^♦=λ; diagram-swapped A2 fundamental coweights average to their half-sum.

items.name: Dominant chamber on a root pairing
items.statement: For an ordered coefficient ring and a root pairing with base b, the closed dominant chamber consists of x with every simple coroot functional nonnegative; the open chamber uses strict positivity. Apply to the flipped pairing for coweights.
items.note: API: Reuse membership, addition and nonnegative scaling. Keep dualization explicit so root and coroot dominance are not interchanged. Tests: Zero belongs to the closed chamber, not its interior in positive rank; an A1 positive coweight is dominant.

items.name: Unique dominant representative and its wall stabilizer
items.statement: For a finite crystallographic root system over a strictly ordered domain with the reduced hypotheses on the pairing and its flip, each Weyl orbit meets the closed dominant chamber in exactly one point; a dominant point’s stabilizer is generated by the simple wall reflections fixing it.
items.note: Read FundamentalDomain.lean at f790474; this does not identify the local reductive W0 with the abstract Weyl group. Apply to the flipped pairing after that separate RG2.1 adapter.

items.name: Integral positive coroot cone
items.statement: The additive monoid of nonnegative integer sums of simple coroots is posRootCone on the flipped root pairing. λ≥_Zμ means λ−μ belongs to this monoid, while rational dominance permits nonnegative rational coefficients.
items.note: API: Reuse the natural-coefficient membership witness; add only comparison adapters for integral/rational coweight spaces. Tests: Zero coefficients must be allowed; in A1 the fundamental coweight α∨/2 lies in the rational positive cone but not in the integral coroot cone.

items.name: Finiteness below a dominant integral weight
items.statement: For the finite crystallographic root-system hypotheses in TauCeti.DominantCone, the dominant integral μ with λ−μ in the positive root monoid form a finite set. Dualize for coweights.
items.note: The exact signature additionally requires finite root index, characteristic zero, a domain, IsRootSystem and IsCrystallographic; integrality is ∀ simple i, ∃n:N, coroot′ i μ=n.

items.name: Shrunken Weyl chamber
items.statement: For every positive root α of the reduced root system attached to Wa remove the critical strip {v:−1<〈v,α〉<0}. A shrunken chamber is a connected component of the complement; w is shrunken when w a lies there.
items.note: API: Root-coordinate membership, alcove criterion, diagram invariance and relation to ordinary Weyl chambers; use the chosen negative base alcove. Tests: In A1 the removed strip is (−1,0); s a=(0,1) is shrunken. In A2 an alcove may avoid some critical strips and meet another; check every positive root, not just simple roots.

items.name: Length-decreasing twisted conjugation
items.statement: w→_{s,σ}s w σ(s) for affine simple s when the target length is at most ℓ(w); →_σ is the generated reflexive-transitive relation. w≈_σw′ means both directions, equivalently an equal-length reduction chain.
items.note: API: Reflexivity, transitivity, preservation of twisted conjugacy, equal-length criterion and σ-equivariance. Tests: s²=1 gives reversible equal-length steps; a strict descent cannot reverse without increasing length.

items.name: Reduction to minimal length
items.statement: For every σ-twisted conjugacy class O in Wtilde and w∈O there exists w′∈O of minimal length with w→_σw′.
items.note: Do not conflate twisted conjugacy with cyclic equivalence; HN14 proof still needs independent source decomposition.

items.name: Minimal-length nonemptiness
items.statement: If w is minimal in its σ-twisted conjugacy class, X_w(b)≠∅ iff wdot∈[b].

items.name: Minimal-length dimension
items.statement: Under the preceding minimal-length and nonemptiness hypotheses, dim X_w(b)=ℓ(w)−〈ν_b,2ρ〉.

items.name: Equal-length reduction preserves dimension
items.statement: If w≈_σw′ then dim X_w(b)=dim X_w′(b) for every b, including empty loci.

items.name: Two-branch reduction formula
items.statement: If s is affine simple and ℓ(s w σ(s))=ℓ(w)−2, then dim X_w(b)=max(dim X_{sw}(b),dim X_{s w σ(s)}(b))+1.
items.note: Export the geometric open/closed pieces and affine-line or punctured-affine-line bundle reductions, not just an equality of numbers.

items.name: Universal comparison after virtual dimension
items.statement: w⇒_σw′ means for every b, dim X_w(b)−d_w(b)≥dim X_w′(b)−d_w′(b). Equivalently nonemptiness of X_w′(b) implies that of X_w(b), and their dimension difference is at least (ℓw+ℓηw−ℓw′−ℓηw′)/2.
items.note: API: Define the relation with an explicit −∞ carrier or the equivalent implication form; prove equivalence and transitivity; define ⇔_σ by mutual comparison. Tests: Empty source/target combinations; reflexivity; κ mismatch cannot be hidden by an undefined subtraction of infinities.

items.name: Equal-length and finite-part comparison
items.statement: If w≈_σw′ and ℓη_σ(w)≤ℓη_σ(w′), then w⇒_σw′; with equal finite-part lengths, w⇔_σw′.

items.name: Demazure product
items.statement: For u,v in a Coxeter/extended affine group, u*v is the unique Bruhat maximum of {a v:a≤u}, equivalently of {a b:a≤u,b≤v}, with the appropriate Ω-component.
items.note: API: Construct the maximum, simple-generator recursion, agreement with ordinary product under length additivity and extension across Ω. Tests: s*s=s while s·s=1; in S3 (s1s2)*s2=s1s2; finite braid relations.

items.name: Associativity and unit of Demazure product
items.statement: (u*v)*w=u*(v*w), and 1*w=w*1=w.

items.name: Bruhat monotonicity of Demazure product
items.statement: If u′≤u and v′≤v then u′*v′≤u*v.

items.name: Demazure support and length factorizations
items.statement: For finite Weyl elements supp(u*v)=supp(u)∪supp(v); moreover ℓ(u*v)=ℓu+ℓ(u⁻¹(u*v))=ℓ((u*v)v⁻¹)+ℓv. Diagram automorphisms preserve *.

items.name: Generic Newton class in an Iwahori double coset
items.statement: B(G)_w={[b]:X_w(b)≠∅} has a unique maximal class [b_w], the generic Newton class of IwdotI; dim X_w(b_w)=ℓw−〈2ρ,ν_bw〉.
items.note: API: Construct the class with its maximality property and Newton-stratum interpretation; no arbitrary maximal choice. Tests: Translation and x t^λ cases; retain κ in maximality comparisons.

items.name: Cordial element
items.statement: w is cordial iff dim X_w(b_w)=d_w(b_w), equivalently ℓw−ℓη_σ(w)=〈ν_bw,2ρ〉−def_G(b_w).
items.note: API: Equivalence of numerical/geometry definitions, class invariance and transport under ⇔_σ. Tests: x t^λ; comparison-equivalent elements share cordiality; no assertion that every element is cordial.

items.name: Cordiality under universal comparison equivalence
items.statement: If w⇔_σw′ then w is cordial iff w′ is cordial.
items.note: Mutual nonemptiness propagation identifies B(G)_w and B(G)_w′ and hence their maximal classes.

items.name: Saturation for cordial elements
items.statement: If w is cordial, [b]≤[b′]≤[b_w] and X_w(b)≠∅, then X_w(b′)≠∅.
items.note: A known nonempty lower endpoint is essential; saturation does not assert every class below [b_w] occurs.

items.name: Dimension for cordial elements
items.statement: For cordial w and any b with X_w(b)≠∅, dim X_w(b)=d_w(b).

items.name: Finite Weyl element times dominant translation is cordial
items.statement: If G is simple quasi-split, λ dominant and x∈W0, then x t^λ is cordial.

items.name: Generic Newton class of x t^λ
items.statement: For the same x and λ, [b_{x t^λ}]=[t^λ].

items.name: Special-parahoric nonemptiness criterion
items.statement: For quasi-split G, a σ-stable special maximal parahoric K containing I, dominant λ and [b]∈B(G), [b]∩K t^λ K≠∅ iff κ(b)=κ(t^λ) and ν_b≤λ^♦.
items.note: The published proof cites Gashi10 Thm1.1 for unramified groups and He14 Thm7.1 for the general case. He15 Thm2.24 is a further reformulation; preserve the characteristic/ramification transport required by these sources.

items.name: Closure does not change the maximal Newton class
items.statement: For an Iwahori double coset, its Bruhat closure has the same maximal σ-conjugacy class as the double coset itself, in the source’s affine flag/Newton geometry.
items.note: Original Vi14 proof not read in this checkpoint; record as a prerequisite, not a verified unrestricted mixed-characteristic assertion.

items.name: Bruhat closure sandwich for x t^λ
items.statement: For λ dominant, closure(I t^λ I)⊂closure(I x t^λ I)⊂closure(I w_S t^λ I)=closure(K t^λ K), where w_S is the longest finite Weyl element and K the associated special parahoric.
items.note: All overbars are essential; the raw disjoint Iwahori double cosets do not contain one another. PDF image checked.

items.name: Translation Newton and length identities
items.statement: In the quasi-split setup ν_{t^λ}=λ^♦ and def(t^λ)=0 for dominant λ; ℓ(t^λ)=〈λ,2ρ〉=〈λ^♦,2ρ〉, η(x t^λ)=x and ℓ(x t^λ)=ℓx+ℓ(t^λ).

items.name: Dominant-chamber cordiality via twisted rotation
items.statement: If w=w_S t^λy, λ dominant and t^λy∈{}^S Wtilde, then w≈_σσ⁻¹(y)w_S t^λ, with equal η-lengths. Thus w is cordial.
items.note: Not every x t^λ is ≈_σ-equivalent to an element in that chamber; do not claim an exhaustive classification.

items.name: Feasible dominant subtraction set is nonempty
items.statement: For dominant integral coweights λ,λ′ in a fixed root-datum lattice, there exists a dominant μ with μ+λ′≥_Zλ. One may use μ=λ−λ′+N·2ρ∨ for N sufficiently large in the semisimple coweight space, retaining any central coordinate separately.
items.note: λ itself need not be feasible because λ′ need not lie in the coroot lattice. The central coordinate is fixed by the root-lattice congruence.

items.name: Common lower bound for two feasible coweights
items.statement: If μ1,μ2 are dominant and μi+λ′≥_Zλ, write μ1−μ2=γ1−γ2 with disjoint simple-coroot supports and nonnegative coefficients. Then μ=μ1−γ1=μ2−γ2 is dominant and μ+λ′≥_Zλ, with μ≤_Zμ1,μ2.
items.note: Use simple coroots, not the printed α in the coweight sums; zero coefficients are allowed. Off-diagonal Cartan entries are nonpositive.

items.name: Least dominant feasible coweight
items.statement: For dominant λ,λ′ the set of dominant μ with μ+λ′≥_Zλ has a unique least element.
items.note: The paper states unique minimal. Complete the argument using a feasible μ0, finiteness of dominant elements below μ0 (pinned Tau Ceti after dualization), a minimal element there, and the common-lower-bound lemma to obtain leastness globally.

items.name: Normalized dominant subtraction
items.statement: λ−domλ′ is the preceding least dominant μ with μ+λ′≥_Zλ.
items.note: API: Feasibility, leastness, characterization by μ+λ′≥_Zλ, lattice congruence, monotonicity in each variable and σ-equivariance. Tests: A1 coweight lattice P∨=Zω∨ with α∨=2ω∨: 0−domω∨=ω∨, not zero; this is a least element in a congruence class, not coordinatewise truncated subtraction.

items.name: Agreement with ordinary dominant difference
items.statement: If λ,λ′ are dominant and λ−λ′ is dominant, then λ−domλ′=λ−λ′.

items.name: Dominant representative bounds normalized subtraction
items.statement: If λ,λ′,λ′′ are dominant and λ′≥_Zλ′′, x∈W0 and μ is the dominant representative of λ−xλ′′, then μ≥_Zλ−domλ′.
items.note: Requires the positive-coroot-difference lemma for a dominant representative and for λ′′−xλ′′, as well as lattice integrality.

items.name: Iterated normalized subtraction
items.statement: For dominant λ,λ1,λ2, (λ−domλ1)−domλ2=λ−dom(λ1+λ2).

items.name: Auxiliary fundamental coweight sum
items.statement: For J⊂S, in the full coweight lattice of the reduced root system define ρ∨_J by 〈ρ∨_J,α_s〉=1 for s∈J and 0 otherwise; let η∨_J be the dominant representative of −σ⁻¹ρ∨_J.
items.note: API: Construct via the dual basis; prove uniqueness, J=∅/S values and diagram equivariance; distinguish full coweight lattice from X_*(T)_Γ0. Tests: For SL2, ρ∨_{s}=α∨/2 is not an SL2 cocharacter; for adjoint A1 it is integral.

items.name: Unresolved integral realization of auxiliary translations
items.statement: The proof uses t^{ρ∨_J} and t^{λ−ρ∨_J} as elements of the working Iwahori–Weyl group. For a general simple quasi-split G this requires an explicit passage to an auxiliary/adjoint coweight lattice and a geometry/dimension descent theorem; it is not automatic in X_*(T)_Γ0.
items.note: UNROUTED G1: false if read as claiming ρ∨_J is always an original cocharacter (SL2). GHN15 §2 plus its 2017 erratum gives only qualified componentwise adjoint comparisons. Resolve the carrier before activating the proposed main route.

items.name: Descent set forces dominant shifted coweight
items.statement: If t^λy∈{}^S Wtilde and J={s∈S:sy<y}, then 〈λ,α_s〉>0 for s∈J and λ−ρ∨_J is dominant in the full coweight lattice.

items.name: Double-flat coweight
items.statement: For w=x t^λy in its normal form and J the left descent set of y, define λ_w^{♭♭}=(λ−ρ∨_J)−domη∨_J=λ−dom(ρ∨_J+η∨_J), in a specified coweight lattice.
items.note: API: Equivalence of the two expressions, dominance, σ-average and compatibility with any adjoint/auxiliary-lattice comparison; retain G1 as a prerequisite. Tests: J=∅ gives λ^{♭♭}=λ; split minuscule λ gives λ^{♭♭}=λ; A1 λ=α∨,y=s gives zero.

items.name: Relative-position orbit and convolution incidence variety
items.statement: O_w={(gI,g wdot I):g∈G(L)}⊂Fl². The triple incidence space consists of (g,g′,g′′) with relative positions (g,g′′)=u,(g′′,g′)=v and optionally (g,g′)=z. Give these their locally closed geometric structures.
items.note: API: Well-defined relative position, diagonal action, fiber products, forgetful projections and bounded models; distinguish points from the representing schemes/perfections. Tests: O_1 is the diagonal; length-additive chains have unique intermediate flag; rank-one convolution has A1 and Gm fibers.

items.name: Length-additive convolution is an isomorphism
items.statement: If ℓ(uv)=ℓu+ℓv, forgetting the intermediate flag identifies the two-step relative-position incidence space with O_{uv}.

items.name: Convolution onto the ordinary-product orbit
items.statement: For u,v∈Wtilde the incidence space with total position uv maps surjectively to O_{uv}; every fiber has dimension at least (ℓu+ℓv−ℓuv)/2.
items.note: Proof by simple-reflection induction and A1/Gm strata; characteristic/perfection transport belongs to the geometry adapter.

items.name: Convolution onto the Demazure-product orbit
items.statement: For u,v∈Wtilde the incidence space with total position u*v maps surjectively to O_{u*v}; every fiber has dimension at least ℓu+ℓv−ℓ(u*v).

items.name: Finite-type fiber lower bound gives total dimension bound
items.statement: For a surjective finite-type morphism X→Y of nonempty finite-type schemes over a field, if every geometric fiber has dimension at least d, then dim X≥dim Y+d. Apply to bounded models, and pass through perfection by a proved dimension comparison.
items.note: The paper uses GW10 Cor.14.116. Its finite union of proper closed subsets needs finiteness of the relevant components; an arbitrary ind-scheme or infinite union cannot replace the finite-type hypothesis.

items.name: Unresolved boundedness and perfect-geometry bridge in the fiber argument
items.statement: For the particular maps X2→X3 and X4→X5 in §5.4, one must justify a finite-type (or perfected finite-type) convolution model over each finite-dimensional irreducible target component, sufficient to apply the preceding fiber-dimension inequality.
items.note: UNROUTED G2: the source writes ⋃_Y Z_Y≠Z without spelling out finiteness. This is a proof-interface obligation, not an assertion that the paper’s conclusion is false. Verify bounded convolution and component hypotheses before routing this bridge.

items.name: Parabolic factors used in the cordial reduction
items.statement: For w=x t^λy shrunken, set J=des_L(y), J′={s:s(λ−ρ∨_J)=λ−ρ∨_J}, and factor η_σ(w)=x′z with x′∈W0^{J′}, z∈W_{J′}.
items.note: API: Name J,J′,x′,z and their length-additive decomposition; identify J′ with zero simple pairings and retain G1. Tests: J′=∅ and J′=S; singular λ−ρ∨_J must not be assumed regular.

items.name: Shrunken-chamber sign and first length cancellation
items.statement: Under those hypotheses xα_j<0 for each j∈J′; consequently ℓ(xz⁻¹)=ℓx−ℓz.
items.note: The root-sign implication cites GH10 §2.3; verify the sign convention against a negative base alcove.

items.name: Dominant γ and its transporter
items.statement: Let β=λ−ρ∨_J+(x′)⁻¹σ⁻¹ρ∨_J. Choose its unique dominant representative γ; let K={s:sγ=γ} and y′∈W0^K with β=y′γ. Then γ≥_Zλ_w^{♭♭}.
items.note: API: Define β,γ,K,y′ with unique representative conventions; derive γ bound from Cor.5.3 and check lattice/Kottwitz compatibility. Tests: γ on a wall has nontrivial K; β=0 forces y′=1, not an arbitrary Weyl element.

items.name: Inversion containment gives length cancellation
items.statement: For the chosen γ,y′, if α>0 and (y′)⁻¹α<0, then 〈y′γ,α〉<0 and x′α<0. Hence ℓ(x′y′)=ℓx′−ℓy′.
items.note: Uses minimality y′∈W0^K to rule out zero pairing, and GH10 Lemma2.6.1 for inversion/length conversion.

items.name: Left minimality and second additive length identity
items.statement: The above y′ belongs to {}^{J′}W0, and ℓ((y′)⁻¹z)=ℓy′+ℓz.

items.name: Two factors w1 and w2
items.statement: With the preceding data define w1=xz⁻¹ t^{λ−ρ∨_J}y′ and w2=(y′)⁻¹z t^{ρ∨_J}y. Then w=w1w2.
items.note: API: Define both factors only after G1 is resolved; prove product, normal-form and length identities. Tests: Rank-one computation; translations in an enlarged lattice require an explicit carrier comparison.

items.name: Length accounting in the two-factor construction
items.statement: ℓw1=ℓ(xz⁻¹)+ℓt^{λ−ρ∨_J}−ℓy′, ℓw2=ℓ((y′)⁻¹z)+ℓt^{ρ∨_J}−ℓy, and ℓw=ℓw1+ℓw2. Also ℓ((y′)⁻¹z)+ℓ(x′y′)=ℓη_σ(w).

items.name: Twisted rotation and X1
items.statement: Length-additive convolution identifies X_w(b) with chains g→_{w1}g1→_{w2}bσ(g). The rotation (g,g1)↦(g1,bσ(g)) gives a universal homeomorphism to X1={g1→_{w2}g2→_{σ(w1)}bσ(g1)}.
items.note: API: Construct maps and Frobenius inverses after perfection; prove universal homeomorphism, nonemptiness and dimension preservation. Tests: A purely inseparable Frobenius map is not automatically an isomorphism on unperfected schemes.

items.name: First constrained correspondence X2→X3
items.statement: Write A=(y′)⁻¹z and B=t^{ρ∨_J}y. Refine X1 as g1→_A g3→_B g2→_{σ(w1)}bσ(g1). X2 imposes (g3,bσg1) of position σ(x′y′t^γ). X3 forgets g2 and splits that last length-additive position into σ(x′y′),σ(t^γ).
items.note: API: Define locally closed inclusions/projections and verify Bσ(w1)=σ(x′y′t^γ), so Prop.5.6 applies. Tests: Ordinary-product fiber bound uses N1=(ℓB+ℓw1−ℓ(x′y′t^γ))/2; no Demazure bound is substituted at this first step.

items.name: First dimension gain
items.statement: X2→X3 is surjective with all fibers of dimension at least N1=(ℓ(t^{ρ∨_J}y)+ℓw1−ℓ(x′y′t^γ))/2; after the boundedness bridge G2, dim X_w(b)≥dim X3+N1.

items.name: Demazure factor a and second correspondence
items.statement: Put a=σ⁻¹((y′)⁻¹z)*(x′y′). Inside X3 let X4 impose total position σ(a) from g1 to g4, and let X5 forget g3. Then X4→X5 uses the Demazure case of Prop.5.6.
items.note: API: Define a, X4,X5 and maps on the same flag carrier; prove σ(a)=A*σ(x′y′). Tests: σ must act on both factors of *; replacing * by ordinary multiplication loses support.

items.name: Support survives the Demazure construction
items.statement: supp_σ(a) contains supp_σ(η_σ(w)), because support of * is a union and supp(x′y′(y′)⁻¹z)⊂supp(x′y′)∪supp((y′)⁻¹z).

items.name: Second dimension gain and final identification
items.statement: After G2, dim X3≥dim X5+ℓη_σ(w)−ℓa. The length-additive map gives X5≅X_{σ(at^γ)}(b), universally homeomorphic to X_{at^γ}(b).

items.name: Nonemptiness and virtual-dimension comparison
items.statement: If X_{at^γ}(b)≠∅, the two surjective correspondences imply X_w(b)≠∅ and dim X_w(b)−dim X_{at^γ}(b)≥(ℓw−ℓ(at^γ)+ℓη_σ(w)−ℓa)/2=d_w(b)−d_{at^γ}(b).

items.name: Reduction to a cordial element
items.statement: For simple quasi-split G and w a shrunken alcove, there exist dominant γ≥_Zλ_w^{♭♭} and a∈W0 with supp_σ(a)⊃supp_σ(η_σ(w)) such that w⇒_σa t^γ.
items.note: Extracted as the paper’s target; G1 and G2 prevent claiming proof closure at this checkpoint.

items.name: Levi alcove condition
items.statement: For σ-stable J⊂S and v∈W0, w is a (J,v,σ)-alcove element if v⁻¹wσ(v)∈Wtilde_J and ({}^{vdot}U_{P_J}(L))∩{}^{wdot}I⊂({}^{vdot}U_{P_J}(L))∩I, with superscripts denoting conjugation.
items.note: API: Define standard Levi/parabolic/unipotent radical using RG2.1; root-subgroup criterion, conjugation conventions, σ-stability and strict variant. Tests: J=S makes the unipotent condition vacuous; conjugates {}^wI are not left cosets wI.

items.name: Levi Kottwitz obstruction
items.statement: If w is a (J,v,σ)-alcove element and κ_{M_J}(v⁻¹wσ(v)) differs from κ_{M_J}(b′) for every b′∈[b]∩M_J(L), then X_w(b)=∅. No basic assumption is needed on b.
items.locator: Theorem 6.3 p.13; GHN15 Corollary3.6.1 with He’s footnote
items.note: GHN15 §3 is stated for tamely ramified quasi-split semisimple groups. Its contraction proof gives this direction without basic b; removing its tame geometry hypotheses still needs justification. Do not import the false nonbasic uniqueness assertion corrected in the erratum.

items.name: Corrected conjugating element for the support obstruction
items.statement: Write w=x t^λy as in §2.2 and put J=supp_σ(σ⁻¹(y)x). GHN15 Lemma3.6.3 makes w a (J,x,σ)-alcove element, and x⁻¹wσ(x)=t^λ yσ(x)=t^λσ(η_σ(w)) belongs to Wtilde_J.
items.note: The printed (J,σ⁻¹(y),σ) and later conjugate use inconsistent inverse conventions. Using the original normal-form left factor x matches the cited lemma and leaves the translation λ unchanged. This is a repair of the proof’s notation, not a change to the theorem.

items.name: Newton vector and Levi Kottwitz comparison
items.statement: For b′∈[b]∩M_J(L), its M_J-dominant ν^M_b′ lies in W0ν_b, and ν_b−ν^M_b′ is a nonnegative rational sum of simple coroots. If its Levi κ equals that of t^λσ(η), then λ^♦−ν^M_b′ lies in the rational span of J-coroots.
items.note: Keep every b′ rather than assuming [b]∩M_J(L) is a single Levi class; the latter requires basic b.

items.name: Emptiness for proper σ-support
items.statement: For w shrunken and λ_w^♦−ν_b having strictly positive coefficient on every simple coroot, if supp_σ(η_σ(w)) is proper then X_w(b)=∅.
items.note: The strict cone cannot lie in the span of a proper σ-stable J after adding ν_b−ν^M_b′. This uses the strict Newton assumption of Thm6.1 even though the first line of §6.2 only repeats the double-flat assumption.

items.name: Basic class below a fixed Kottwitz fibre
items.statement: For κ=κ(w), choose τ∈Ω representing the basic class with that κ. If κ(b)=κ, then [τdot]≤[b].
items.note: Uniqueness is for the σ-class/basic class, not a unique element τ of Ω.

items.name: Kottwitz preservation through cordial reduction
items.statement: For the constructed γ,a, κ(t^γ)=κ(w); γ−λ is a sum of coroot terms and a (σ−1)-coboundary in the chosen coweight lattice, hence vanishes in the required σ-coinvariants after the carrier comparison.
items.note: Needs G1: computing in an enlarged lattice does not alone prove equality in the original Ω_σ.

items.name: Basic nonemptiness used for the reduced element
items.statement: The proof needs X_{a t^γ}(τdot)≠∅ for the specific dominant γ and full-σ-support a constructed in Thm5.5, with κ(τ)=κ(t^γ). The cited He15 Thm2.27 applies only when a t^γ has a shrunken alcove.
items.note: UNROUTED G3: the construction need not produce a shrunken a t^γ. In split adjoint A2 take λ=ω2∨=(0,1), y=1, x=s2s1. Then J=∅, J′={s1}, x′=s2, z=s1, γ=λ, y′=1 and a=s1*s2=s1s2. On the base alcove with u<0,v<0,u+v>−1, w maps (u,v) to (v−1,1−u−v), outside every critical strip; a t^γ maps it to (1−u−v,u), whose second coordinate is in (−1,0). Both finite parts have full support. Thus He15 Thm2.27 cannot directly be applied to this constructed a t^γ. Supply a more general basic-seed theorem or alter the reduction; this does not disprove the main theorem. The earlier A1 suspicion was rejected after checking the exact sign convention.

items.name: Lower dimension bound by cordial saturation
items.statement: Assume the main hypotheses, the reduction w⇒a t^γ and its basic nonemptiness input. Then γ^♦≥(λ_w^{♭♭})^♦≥ν_b and equal κ give [τ]≤[b]≤[t^γ]. Cordial saturation makes X_{at^γ}(b) nonempty with dimension d_{at^γ}(b), hence dim X_w(b)≥d_w(b).

items.name: Main nonemptiness criterion
items.statement: Under the paper’s standing simple quasi-split G/F hypothesis, let b∈G(L), w∈Wtilde with w a shrunken, λ_w^♦−ν_b∈Σ_{α∈Δ}Q_{>0}α∨ and (λ_w^{♭♭})^♦≥ν_b. Then X_w(b)≠∅ iff κ(b)=κ(w) and supp_σ(η_σ(w))=S.
items.note: Both Newton hypotheses are retained; no claim for all w or all [b]≤[t^λ]. The broad scope remains a target pending G1–G3 and source-hypothesis transport.

items.name: Main dimension formula
items.statement: With all hypotheses of the preceding main criterion and its two nonemptiness conditions, dim X_w(b)=(ℓw+ℓη_σ(w)−def_G(b))/2−〈ν_b,ρ〉.

items.name: Minuscule exception in the two Newton bounds
items.statement: If G is split and λ_w is minuscule, then λ_w^{♭♭}=λ_w; therefore the weak double-flat bound alone does not imply strict positivity of λ_w^♦−ν_b.
items.note: A nonzero dominant difference in an irreducible root system lies in the strictly positive rational simple-coroot cone, but zero is a necessary exception.

items.name: Basic-class double-flat bound
items.statement: For basic [b] with κ(b)=κ(w), (λ_w^{♭♭})^♦≥ν_b in the setup where the double-flat carrier/Kottwitz compatibility is established.

items.name: Two-rho sufficient Newton bound
items.statement: If λ_w^♦≥ν_b+2ρ∨, then (λ_w^{♭♭})^♦≥ν_b and λ_w^♦−ν_b is strictly positive on all simple-coroot coefficients. The argument uses 2ρ∨−ρ∨_J−η∨_J≥0 in the rational coroot cone.
items.note: λ_w−2ρ∨ itself need not be dominant; only its σ-average is constrained.

items.name: Effective-region nonemptiness criterion
items.statement: For G simple quasi-split, w a shrunken and λ_w^♦≥ν_b+2ρ∨, X_w(b)≠∅ iff κ(b)=κ(w) and supp_σ(η_σ(w))=S.

items.name: Effective-region dimension formula
items.statement: Under the preceding Cor.6.4 hypotheses and nonemptiness, dim X_w(b)=d_w(b).

items.name: Sufficiently large fundamental ray
items.statement: For an irreducible root system and fixed b, if λ_w=nω∨ is an allowed integral multiple of a fundamental coweight and n is sufficiently large, then λ_w^♦≥ν_b+2ρ∨.
items.note: Only multiples lying in the actual cocharacter lattice are allowed. This supplies the Newton bound, not the separate shrunken-alcove assumption.

items.name: Necessary Hodge–Newton conditions
items.statement: If X_w(b)≠∅, then κ(b)=κ(w) and ν_b≤λ_w^♦.

items.name: Levi reduction for proper support
items.statement: For w in a shrunken chamber with proper J=supp_σ(η_σ(w)), use the appropriate (J,v,σ)-alcove and Hodge–Newton decomposition to reduce the ADLV to suitable Levi ADLV data; recheck Theorem6.1’s hypotheses on each simple Levi factor before applying it.
items.note: The side remark is not a theorem that all classes satisfying Mazur’s inequality are covered, nor an unrestricted equality of G- and Levi-varieties without the required quotient/components. GHKR10 Thm2.1.4 and GHN15 Thm3.3.1 require separate decomposition.

items.name: Corrected adjoint comparison on connected components
items.statement: In equal characteristic with char(k) not dividing |π1(G_ad)|, G→G_ad identifies each selected connected component of its affine flag variety with the corresponding component for G_ad; a global immersion requires injectivity of the map on component groups. The induced componentwise ADLV comparison is GHN15 Cor.2.2.2.
items.note: The erratum explicitly removes the automatic injectivity claim. In mixed characteristic the cited original passage only establishes a set-theoretic comparison; dimension requires the later perfect-geometry bridge.

items.name: Levi class uniqueness only for a basic G-class
items.statement: If [b] is basic and J is σ-stable, [b]∩M_J(L) contains at most one σ-conjugacy class of M_J(L). This statement is false without basic b.
items.locator: GHN15 erratum Proposition0.0.2; He21 Thm6.3 footnote
items.note: Counterexample GL2 with diagonal Levi: diag(t,1),diag(1,t) are G-σ-conjugate but not torus-σ-conjugate.

prerequisites.citation: Görtz–He–Nie, P-alcoves and nonemptiness of affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties (2015), and 2017 erratum
prerequisites.why: Read §§2.1–2.5 and §§3.1–3.6, plus all three erratum pages. Supplies adjoint/inner-form comparison and Levi obstruction. Tame ramification, equal-characteristic prime restrictions and componentwise comparison must be preserved. Erratum: https://www.esaga.uni-due.de/f/ulrich.goertz/pdf/Erratum-GHN.pdf .

prerequisites.citation: Görtz–He, Dimensions of affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties in affine flag varieties (2010)
prerequisites.why: Read author PDF pp.6–7 for relative-position convolution and Prop.2.5.2; the remaining induction and Lemma2.6.1 proof need a dedicated pass. Supplies actual A1/Gm geometry and length-to-inversion lemmas.

prerequisites.citation: Milićević–Viehmann, Generic Newton points and the Newton poset in Iwahori-double cosets (2020)
prerequisites.why: Read pp.2,8–9: Thm1.1, Cor3.12, Def3.14 and Thm3.16 proof. Newton purity, maximal chain lengths and completion geometry behind cordial saturation remain a prerequisite subtree, not assumed theorem fields.

prerequisites.citation: He, Hecke algebras and p-adic groups (2015 survey)
prerequisites.why: Read pp.37–38: Thm2.27 has a shrunken hypothesis; Thm2.30 concerns I-normalized Newton-stratum dimension. Trace Thm2.23/2.24 and general ramified/perfect-geometry comparisons before closing the upper-bound/Mazur/basic-seed imports.

prerequisites.citation: He–Nie, Minimal length elements of extended affine Weyl groups (2014)
prerequisites.why: He21 Thm3.1 imports §2. Exact twisted reduction proof and its affine root-datum generality are not fully read here; atlas basic Coxeter theory does not supply this theorem.

prerequisites.citation: He, Geometric and homological properties of affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties (2014)
prerequisites.why: He21 Thm3.2, Prop3.3, Thm4.4 and the upper bound use minimal-length geometry, Deligne–Lusztig reduction, Thm7.1 and Cor10.4. Full original proof acquisition/decomposition remains; do not replace the mixed/perfect extension with a set bijection.

prerequisites.citation: Viehmann, Truncations of level 1 of elements in the loop group of a reductive group (2014)
prerequisites.why: Cor5.6 is used in the maximal-Newton closure sandwich; the original proof and characteristic range remain to be read.

prerequisites.citation: He, A subalgebra of a 0-Hecke algebra (2009)
prerequisites.why: He21 §3.4 cites Lemma1 for the Demazure maximum. DOI 10.1016/j.jalgebra.2009.04.003 verified from the author institutional record; full proof not read. GH10 Lemma2.5.1 restates the required maximum and support formulas.

Generic fiber-dimension theorem in He21 §5.4. The exact cited edition/page has not been acquired; use a verified equivalent finite-type theorem and prove applicability to the bounded/perfect correspondence.

prerequisites.citation: Görtz–Haines–Kottwitz–Reuman, Affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties in affine flag varieties (2010)
prerequisites.why: Thm2.1.4 supplies the split Hodge–Newton decomposition in §6.5. Whole source not read; the proper-support side remark requires exact Levi components/quotients and hypotheses.

routes.reason: The completion/Frobenius adapter supports the already owned topology of local rational points; import finite unramified field theory from Tau Ceti without replanning it.
The relative/affine root datum and its actual lattice belong to the local reductive root-data owner.
The existing building/parahoric stages own alcoves and Iwahori models.
The Iwahori–Weyl group, normal forms, length conventions and double-coset computations refine the existing decomposition stage.
B(G) and the algebraic J_b are already owned here; defect is a direct rank interface on that group.
These are the existing κ/ν, order and central/Levi functoriality targets, with the nonbasic warning made explicit.

The existing stages explicitly own affine flag/perfect flag geometry and relative-position strata. Add these convolution and adjoint-comparison interfaces there; do not rebuild Satake or shtuka diamonds.
The finite-type scheme dimension lemma is general scheme-morphism infrastructure. Its application to the ind/perfect correspondences remains G2.

routes.title: Root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan-Killing classification, Part II: dominant subtraction and Demazure reduction
routes.reason: The upstream roadmap owns chambers, Coxeter presentation, exchange/Matsumoto and basic Bruhat order. It does not state the Demazure monoid, least dominant subtraction or affine twisted minimal-length reduction; add only those extensions, consuming the pinned chamber/Bruhat/positive-cone APIs.
routes.brief: Import root systems, Weyl groups, and the Cartan-Killing classification (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/RootSystems), the existing weight-lattice interfaces from representations of semisimple Lie algebras, highest weight theory, and the Weyl formulas (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/LieHighestWeight), and local relative/affine root adapters from ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.1/RG2.4. Do not re-plan any upstream layer; reconcile their conflicting prose about lattice ownership by using the existing pinned root-datum carrier. Construct only the missing parabolic-representative/support adapters and Demazure product, with maximum characterization, simple recursion, associativity, monotonicity, support union and ordinary-product comparison. Prove the HN14 reduction-to-minimal-length theorem for affine twisted conjugacy. For an explicit full coweight lattice prove nonemptiness, lower-directedness and leastness of the dominant subtraction feasible set; export Prop.5.1, Cor.5.3 and the exact identity (λ−domλ1)−domλ2=λ−dom(λ1+λ2). Supply ρ∨_J and η∨_J on this full lattice, the root-sign/length lemmas used in (5.1)–(5.4), the minuscule exception and the 2ρ∨ bound. Do not identify the full lattice with the cocharacters of every G; G1 must be settled by an explicit comparison. Test A1 parity in P∨/Q∨, singular A2 representatives, s*s=s, diagram automorphisms, non-simply-laced dual root data and strict versus weak dominance. Every definition needs APIs and genuine unit examples. Suggested future Lean home: TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coxeter/Demazure.lean and TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/DominantSubtraction.lean; no Lean implementation is supplied in this paper job.

routes.title: Hecke correspondences and local shtuka cohomology, Part II: cordial elements and affine Deligne–Lusztig dimensions
routes.reason: HS2 owns local shtuka moduli but none of its layers proves classical Iwahori-level affine Deligne–Lusztig nonemptiness or dimension formulas. This is a continuation in the local Frobenius-modification direction, sharing GS0 geometry and BG invariants. It is not a new copy of affine flags, B(G), Satake or general Hecke functors.
routes.brief: Import Hecke correspondences and local shtuka cohomology (HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas, HS0/HS2), geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve (GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS0:loop-geometry/GS0:Witt-geometry), Bun_G and Newton strata (BunGAndNewtonStrata BG0/BG1), ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.1–RG2.4, SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 and the proposed RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. Keep classical equal-characteristic ADLV schemes and mixed-characteristic perfect ADLV spaces separate from local shtuka diamonds; an actual comparison is needed where used. Construct X_w(b), η_σ, virtual dimension, reduction relations, generic Newton classes, cordiality, double-flat coweights and Levi alcoves. Cover split parts of Theorems2.1/3.1/3.2, Proposition3.3, MV cordial saturation with a known nonempty lower endpoint, and Theorem4.2: x t^λ is cordial with [b_xtλ]=[t^λ]. Prove the precise two-correspondence Theorem5.5, retaining every lattice, finite-type and perfection hypothesis. Final targets: for simple quasi-split G, shrunken w, λ_w^♦−ν_b strictly positive on every simple coroot and (λ_w^{♭♭})^♦≥ν_b, X_w(b) is nonempty exactly when κ(b)=κ(w) and supp_σ(η_σ(w))=S, and then dim=(ℓw+ℓη_σ(w)−def_G(b))/2−〈ν_b,ρ〉. Also prove Cor.6.4 with λ_w^♦≥ν_b+2ρ∨ and the separate shrunken hypothesis. Gate execution on G1–G3: auxiliary/adjoint lattice realization, bounded/perfect fiber-dimension comparison, and a basic-seed theorem covering the constructed element (the explicit A2 example shows it need not be shrunken). Preserve the tame/good-characteristic restrictions of cited inputs until broader transport is proved. Use the corrected (J,x,σ) in §6.2, all overbars in §4.3, and the GHN erratum. Add basic/minuscule/wall/σ-twisted/rank-one and nonbasic-Levi tests; never infer all classes below the maximal Newton point from saturation alone. Suggested future Lean home: TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AffineDeligneLusztig/{Basic,Reduction,Cordial,Dimension}.lean. This checkpoint is a design brief, not a verified proof closure or a Lean implementation.
